transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. A friend of mine noticed how much I've been struggling and suggested I should come in to get checked out.
Have you ever experienced periods of low mood or lack of energy like this in the past, or is this the first time you are feeling this way?

No, this isn't the first time, as these ups and downs have been happening off and on for about a year now. This current low, drained feeling has actually been hanging over me for most of the past eleven months, with only brief breaks when I get those highly energetic, revved-up bursts.
During those highly energetic, revved-up bursts, how long do they typically last, and do they ever lead to risky behaviors or cause problems in your daily life?

Those high-energy periods usually last for about a week or so. During those times, I get pretty impulsive and go on online shopping sprees for tech gear, putting way too much on our credit cards. I also get really snappy and easily irritated with my coworkers or wife if they try to slow me down or question my ideas.
During your low periods, do you experience other symptoms like changes in your sleep or appetite, feelings of hopelessness, or trouble concentrating that last continuously for at least two weeks?

Yes, during these low stretches I feel completely hollow and hopeless, and I'll toss and turn all night or wake up at 3 a.m. unable to get back to sleep. I've also been skipping meals to the point where my pants are loose, and this entire slump has been dragging on continuously for most of the past eleven months.

Based on the patient's description of the depressive phase, the symptoms (hollow/hopeless feelings, significant weight loss, and persistent insomnia) are severe and have lasted continuously for 11 months, which qualifies as a major depressive episode. Additionally, the high periods last for a week and cause significant impairment (credit card debt, relationship strain), which represents a hypomanic or manic episode. Because the episodes meet the full criteria for major depressive and hypomanic/manic episodes, F34.0 (Cyclothymia) is ruled out, leaving F31 (Bipolar affective disorder) as the definitive diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a pattern of alternating mood states over the past year. He is currently experiencing a prolonged depressive episode lasting approximately 11 months, characterized by depressed mood, loss of energy, loss of interest, insomnia, and decreased appetite. He also reports distinct periods lasting about a week characterized by high energy, irritability, and impulsive spending. This presentation of both depressive and manic/hypomanic symptoms meets the criteria for Bipolar Affective Disorder.
